thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: KV cache backpressure detected in us-west-2 — continuous-batching window > 95th pct for 6m, eviction rate spiked x8. auto-mitigation attempted (per-cust throttle) — check #eng-sre runbook.

nina (oncall): on it, reading metrics now. is there a clear customer slice?

dan: seeing a small group of heavy writers from cust:ACME_CORP and a regional burst from us-west-2a. paging due to downstream latency for gen endpoints.

leah: adding context — we rolled batch-window increase last night to 48ms to reduce cost. looks like prefetched KV chains are amplifying for long seqlen requests.

nina (oncall): ok, first move: revert the batch-window change to 32ms for all hosts in us-west-2. can we push a runtime flag quick?

dan: I can toggle the flag. plan: 1) enable per-region soft rollback 2) kick a 1% canary for 5m 3) expand to 25% then full.

sre-lead: +1 on canary. also prepare per-customer override for ACME_CORP while we validate. CS: please notify ACME that we're investigating latency.

cs-rep: pinged acct team, sending proactive note to ACME that we're investigating a performance spike.

nina (oncall): dan, paste the flag command here. include the safe rollback command.

dan: here's the CLI I'm using:

```
redwoodctl feature-flag set batch_window --value 32 --scope region:us-west-2 --actor oncall-nina --reason "rollback after kv amplification"
redwoodctl feature-flag set batch_window --value 32 --scope customer:ACME_CORP --actor oncall-nina --reason "per-cust mitigation"
redwoodctl rollout canary batch_window --scope region:us-west-2 --percent 1 --duration 5m
```

leah: also toggling continuous-batch-enabled=false for the worst hosts (runtime label prefetch-hot). small test to ensure requests don't thrash the KV hot keys.

incident-bot: NOTE: This thread triggered a P1 page at 3000000005. On-call: nina (oncall). Pager duty runbook: KV_BACKPRESSURE_V2.

nina (oncall): executing canary now. pushing 1%. will monitor eviction rate and tail latency (p99 gen).

deploy-bot: ROLL STARTED: canary rollout 1% for flag batch_window -> 32 in us-west-2 at 3000000068 (initiated by dana). status: started.

leah: early signs — eviction rate dropping for canary hosts. p50 latency improved slightly, p99 still noisy.

dan: expanding to 25% after 3m if no regression.

nina (oncall): CS: ACME reported elevated error rate ~3% for generator endpoints. we've applied per-cust override to 32ms; confirm if that helps on your side.

cs-rep: ACME acknowledges override applied, they're running tests. will update in 10m.

incident-bot: METRIC UPDATE: eviction_rate(us-west-2) -40% since canary. continuous-batch window median reduced from 46ms -> 33ms.

leah: big follow-up: there's a secondary pattern where long chat sessions with repeated tool-calls build large KV chains — we should apply conservative KV-prefetch limit for sessions > 2k tokens. adding a temporary guard.

nina (oncall): rolling canary to 25% now. if green in 5m, full region.

deploy-bot: ROLL UPDATE: expanded to 25% at 3000000185.

dan: full region rollout now. also created per-customer override flag to pin ACME to stable profile until fix lands.

deploy-bot: ROLL COMPLETE: batch_window=32 applied to us-west-2 at 3000000250. per-customer override for ACME_CORP set.

nina (oncall): monitoring long tail. eviction and throttle alarms cleared for now. marking immediate customer-facing impact as "partial" since some requests still degraded during spike window.

cs-rep: ACME confirms errors dropped to ~0.2% after override. thanking the team.

sre-lead: good work. next actions: 1) postmortem run (owners: leah + dan) 2) short-term: implement prefetch cap for sessions>2k tokens (leah) 3) long-term: redesign batch-window estimator to account for seqlen distribution (eng-runtime).

nina (oncall): leaving handoff to day shift. @sre-lead I'm adding runbook notes and the exact commands used into the incident ticket.

sre-lead: thanks. also create a customer follow-up note template for CS so they can send a concise RCA.

leah: created quick PR for prefetch cap, test in staging now.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: P1 resolved at 3000000358. summary: KV cache amplification due to batch-window increase + long-sequence prefetch chains. mitigation: regional batch_window rollback + per-customer override while fix deploys.

nina (oncall): closing thread — handoff complete. we'll collect logs, diag artifacts, and timeline for the postmortem.
